messages.subject: ggplot
parts:
Dear All,

library(raster)
library(ggplot2)
r <- raster(nrows=10, ncols=10); r <- setValues(r, 1:ncell(r))
r1 <- raster(nrows=10, ncols=10);r1 <- setValues(r1, 1:ncell(r))
r2 <- raster(nrows=10, ncols=10);r2 <- setValues(r1, 1:ncell(r))
st1=stack(r,r1,r2)
res=mean(st1)

either 
gplot(res)+geom_raster(aes(fill=value))

or
plot(res)

This works perfectly. 
I need to put cross (or anything) on each pixel where at least 2 of the rasters agree on sign.

Do you have any idea?
thanks,
Bic

messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: ggplot
parts:
You need to multiply the rasters together and then check for sign using ifelse. See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/32893939/determining-if-two-columns-contain-either-a-negative-and-positive-value-in-r

library(raster)
library(ggplot2)
r1 <- raster(nrows=10, ncols=10);r1 <- setValues(r, sample(-10:10, ncell(r1), replace=T))
r2 <- raster(nrows=10, ncols=10);r2 <- setValues(r1, sample(-10:10, ncell(r2), replace=T))
r3 <- raster(nrows=10, ncols=10);r3 <- setValues(r2, sample(-10:10, ncell(r3), replace=T))


#Take mean
avg <- mean(r1,r2,r3)


#multiply rasters together, matching signs will end up positive
r4 <- r * r2
r5 <- r2 * r3
r6 <- r1 * r3

#compare for sign
sign <- ifelse(values(r4) > 0 | values(r5) > 0 | values(r6) > 0, 0, 1)

#extract the cell values
crd <- as.data.frame(coordinates(res))
crd[,3] <- sign

#delete the rows where val is 0
i <- which(crd[,3] == 0)
crd <- crd[-i,]


plot(avg)
points(crd, pch=3, cex=5)

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: ggplot
parts:
The ifelse() function here is pretty inefficient - there is a built in sign() function that should be a fair bit faster and more robust. For example, the solution above will not work when the rasters agree on 0. 

In general, if you are using ifelse(), there is probably a more efficient solution. See the discussion here for details: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Performance.html
